## Natural history notes

A medium-sized wild canid characterized by a slender grayish-brown body, pointed ears, narrow muzzle, bushy tail, and alert, dog-like appearance. In Florida, Coyotes are now widespread in forests, ranchlands, prairies, wetlands, suburbs, agricultural areas, parks, and urban edges, using a wide range of habitats as long as food and cover are available. They are adaptable omnivores, feeding on rodents, rabbits, insects, fruit, carrion, and occasionally birds or reptiles, while usually avoiding people and being most active at dawn, dusk, and night.
